top_choice_rationale: P001 (Melitz and Helpman, firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting) is the only award proposal on the slate, and I rank it above no award. Melitz (2003) is an identifiable originating model. Its qualitative predictions (selection into exporting, exporter productivity premia, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation) have been tested in firm and customs data across many countries for more than twenty years. Helpman's work with Melitz and Yeaple on exporting versus FDI makes the two-name credit coherent. A citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism and the gains-from-trade channel is accurate to what was established. The main residual risks are the priority of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum and Yeaple, and the dependence of welfare-gain magnitudes on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity. A tightly worded citation reduces the first without removing it, and neither is serious enough to prefer no award. This is my own assessment of discovery, maturity and attribution, not a count of support.
recusal_note: Profile-based connections, disclosed and not adjudicated: my field (industrial organisation and international trade, including exporters, pricing and firm-level data) is adjacent to the B048 mechanism, which could make me overconfident about its evidence. I co-authored with committee colleagues John Hassler and Tore Ellingsen on price-setting work unrelated to any candidate. My spouse is Magdalena Andersson, a Swedish politician, which is a public fact with no apparent bearing on these candidates. No tie to Melitz or Helpman is apparent from my profile.
